scene: Arlequino plays the instrumental guitar piece Asturias to accompany a beast-army endurance drill after Borga allows him to try. The music gives the group a strong pulse, but its accelerations and dynamic shifts are not perfectly suited to drill cadence: several fighters begin matching it too aggressively and the instructor corrects them to keep form. The skeptical instructor does not become a fan, but allows the piece to continue because it helps focus more than it disrupts. Borga observes that the idea can work if music follows the training rather than turning training into a show. No money is collected; this is not a paid/public busking performance.

knowledge.borga: heard Asturias here and saw its effect on one training group
knowledge.others: only those physically present can know this performance directly
